text:
People think algos remove emotion from trading.

They don't. They just move it.

The emotion shows up when:
• The algo hits a drawdown and you want to switch it off
• It misses a big move and you want to "improve" it
• It has a great month and you want to double the size
• Live results lag the backtest and you start tweaking parameters every week

Every one of those decisions is human, and that's where most algo traders lose money.

What helps:
→ Decide in advance when you'll pause, scale or retire a strategy
→ Review performance on a fixed schedule, not after every trade
→ Change strategies in versions, with a proper test each time
→ Have someone you trust challenge your decisions

The algo carries out the plan. Discipline is still your job.

Algo traders: what's the hardest moment for you not to interfere?
